info.title: Navixy Dashboards API
info.summary: Read the dashboards of a workspace and what their panels show for a period.
info.description:
The Dashboards API returns the data of Navixy Dashboards. It lists the dashboards that an access token may read, with their periods, and returns what every panel of a dashboard shows for a period.

**Requests.** Every operation is a `POST` request with a JSON body. Every body includes `timeZone`, an IANA time zone such as `Europe/Berlin`. The API writes every date and time of the response in that time zone.

**Authentication.** Send an access token in the `Authorization` header: the word `Bearer`, a space, and the token. Your app gets the token by exchanging a Navixy API key. The token gives access to one workspace, and every response has the data of that workspace only.

**Errors.** An error response has an HTTP status other than 2xx and a JSON body with a `code`, a `message`, and sometimes `details`. Check the `code` field in your app: `message` is text for a person and can change. HTTP 401 and HTTP 406 have no body.

servers.description: Navixy production server of your region

region.description: The region of your organization: `eu` for the European Union, `us` for the United States.

post.description: Returns the current time in your time zone and the dashboards that the token may read, each with the IDs of its periods. Call it first: the dashboard codes and the period IDs are the values that Get dashboard data accepts. It reads no panel data, so it doesn't count toward the daily limit of dashboard reads.

200.description: The current time and the dashboards that the token may read.

400.description: The body can't be accepted. `invalid_tool_call` names the wrong fields in `details`: a missing or invalid `timeZone`, a body that isn't a JSON object, or a field that the operation doesn't accept. A body that isn't JSON at all returns `bad_request`.

example.message: The tool call cannot be run as it is.

details.timeZone: the user's IANA time zone, such as Europe/Madrid, not an offset

post.description:
Returns the dashboard data: what every panel of one dashboard shows for a period. Values are in the units of the data, such as kilometers and hours, and times are in your time zone. A table returns 50 rows at most, and a line chart returns a summary of each line and up to 48 points. A panel that the dashboard data doesn't include, or whose data couldn't be read, has an `unavailable` text instead of data.

Each request counts toward a limit of about 250 dashboard reads for each API key in a workspace in 24 hours, from the moment that Navixy accepts it, whatever happens next.

200.description: The dashboard data. The example is Live status in a workspace without assets, shortened to 4 panels.

panels.title: Total assets
panels.description: Total number of unique fleet assets registered for the selected client.

panels.title: Asset locations
panels.unavailable: each asset's last position on a map, whose coordinates Fleet details answers

panels.title: Connection
panels.description:
Breakdown of the fleet by current connection status.
Online: Status is online and a message was received within the last 6 minutes.
Offline: The last message is older than 2 days or missing entirely.
GPS not updated: Message received less than 6 minutes ago, but online conditions are not met.
Other: The last message was received between 6 minutes and 2 days ago.

panels.title: Average and max speed
panels.description: Average and maximum speed over the last 24 hours.

400.description: The body can't be accepted. `invalid_tool_call` names the wrong fields in `details`: `timeZone`, a `dashboard` that the token can't read, a `range` that the dashboard doesn't have, a `previous` that isn't `true` or `false`, or a field that the operation doesn't accept. A wrong `timeZone` is reported alone, before the other fields are checked. A body that isn't JSON at all returns `bad_request`.

example.message: The tool call cannot be run as it is.

429.description: The API key has read about 250 dashboards in this workspace in the last 24 hours. Nothing was read. Retry when the oldest of those reads is more than 24 hours old.

example.message: You have read as many dashboards as a day allows. Please try again later.

503.description: The dashboard can't be read now: Navixy is reading as many dashboards as it can at once, or the read took too long. A refusal because Navixy is busy doesn't count toward the daily limit, and a read that took too long does. A slow read can also end with an HTTP 5xx error without a JSON body, and can still run on the server for a while. Retry any 5xx response after some seconds, and wait longer after each failure.

example.message: A dashboard cannot be read right now. Please try again later.

bearerAuth.description: The access token that your app gets by exchanging a Navixy API key. It's the same token that Navixy GraphQL API accepts.

Unauthorized.description: The request has no token, or the token is invalid or expired. The response has no body. Exchange the API key again and repeat the request with the new token.

Forbidden.description: The token is valid, but the request is refused. `code` says why: `product_not_enabled` when the workspace or the token's role doesn't include Dashboards, `insufficient_rights` when the role doesn't grant the `dashboards-standard` feature, `roles_unresolved` when Navixy couldn't read the roles, and `token_incomplete` when the token's organization, workspace, or API key is missing or invalid.

example.message: The Dashboards product is not enabled.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body isn't sent as JSON. Send it with `Content-Type: application/json`.

example.message: This address does not accept this content type.

InternalError.description: The request failed in Navixy. Retry it later.

example.message: Something went wrong on our side. Please try again.

TimeZone.description: Your time zone, as an IANA time zone name such as `Europe/Madrid`. The response writes every time in it. `UTC` is accepted, and its times end in `Z`. Fixed offsets such as `+01:00`, `UTC+2`, or `Etc/GMT+2` aren't, because they don't follow daylight saving time.

DashboardList.description: The current time and the dashboards that the token may read, with their periods.

now.description: The current time in `timeZone`, as RFC 3339 text with the offset, to the second. In `UTC`, it ends in `Z`.

timeZone.description: The time zone of the request.

dashboards.description: The dashboards that the token may read, in the order of the tabs in Navixy Dashboards. Empty when the role grants none.

DashboardPeriods.description: A dashboard that the token may read, with the IDs of its periods.

code.description: The dashboard's code, the `dashboard` value of Get dashboard data: `live_status`, `trips`, or `conditions`.

ranges.description: The IDs of the dashboard's periods, the `range` values of Get dashboard data. Empty on Live status, which has no periods.

dashboard.description: The code of a dashboard from the `dashboards` list of List dashboards and periods.

range.description: The ID of one of the dashboard's periods, such as `7d` for the last 7 days. Required on Trips and Conditions. Leave it out on Live status, which has no periods.

previous.description: `true` reads the period of the same length right before the period in `range`, to compare 2 periods. Only with `range`. Default `false`.

DashboardData.description: What every panel of one dashboard shows for a period.

range.description: The period's ID. `null` on Live status.

previous.description: `true` when the data covers the period before `range`.

from.description: The start of the period, in the request's time zone, as RFC 3339 text with the offset. `null` on Live status.

to.description: The end of the period, in the same form. `null` on Live status.

panels.description: Every panel of the dashboard, in the order of its definition.

Panel.description: What one panel shows. A panel with data has `fields`, and then `rows` or, for a line chart, `series`. A panel without data has `unavailable` instead.

id.description: The panel's ID, unique in its dashboard.

type.description: How Navixy Dashboards draws the panel: `kpi`, `piechart`, `barchart`, `linechart`, `table`, or `map`. Treat it as text, because a later version can add types.

description.description: What the panel shows and how Navixy calculates it. Absent when the panel has none or has no data.

fields.description: The values of each row or line, with their units.

rows.description: The rows, 50 at most. Each row has one value for each of `fields`: a number in the field's unit, text, or `null`.

rowsLeftOut.description: How many rows after the first 50 the dashboard data leaves out. A table reads 1,000 rows at most, so this is 950 at most. Absent when it leaves out none.

series.description: For a line chart, one item for each line.

unavailable.description: Why the panel has no data here: the dashboard data doesn't include the panel, the panel has no data source, or its data couldn't be read.

PanelField.description: A value of a panel's rows or lines, with its unit.

key.description: The key of the value in each row or line.

label.description: The name of the value in Navixy Dashboards. Absent when the panel shows no name for it.

unit.description: The unit of the value. Absent for text, times, counts, and plain numbers.

x-enumDescriptions.h: Hours as a decimal number, to 2 decimals: 1.5 is 1 hour 30 minutes.
x-enumDescriptions.%: Percent, to 1 decimal, where 100 is the whole.
x-enumDescriptions.°: Degrees: a latitude or a longitude to 5 decimals, or a heading clockwise from north.

Series.description: One line of a line chart. The key of the panel's first text field, such as `asset`, has the name of the line, and is absent on a chart with one line. `points` is the number of points that the line has, and `times` gives the time of each point in `values`. Each value field has a `ValueSummary`.

points.description: How many rows the line has in the period.

times.description: The time of each point, in the request's time zone. 48 at most: over a long period, each point is the average of a part of the period, at the start of the part. A line has a point only where it has data, so 2 lines can have `times` of different lengths. Match the points of 2 lines by their time, not by position.

ValueSummary.description: One value of a line, in its field's unit. `null` when the line has no point with this value.

first.description: The first value in the period.

last.description: The last value in the period.

mean.description: The average of all the rows, rounded to the decimals of the unit, and to 2 decimals at most.

values.description: The value at each of `times`. `null` where the line has data at that time but no value for this field.

Error.description: The body of every error response except 401 and 406.

code.description: What went wrong. Check this value in your app.

x-enumDescriptions.invalid_tool_call: 400. A field of the body is missing or wrong. `details` names the wrong fields. A wrong `timeZone` is reported alone, before the other fields are checked.
x-enumDescriptions.product_not_enabled: 403. The workspace or the token's role doesn't include Dashboards.
x-enumDescriptions.insufficient_rights: 403. The role doesn't grant the `dashboards-standard` feature.
x-enumDescriptions.roles_unresolved: 403. Navixy couldn't read the token's roles. Contact Navixy support.
x-enumDescriptions.token_incomplete: 403. The token's organization, workspace, or API key is missing or invalid. `details.claim` names which. Exchange the API key again, and contact Navixy support if the error repeats.
x-enumDescriptions.not_found: 404. The path starts with `/api/tools/`, but no operation has this name.
x-enumDescriptions.method_not_allowed: 405. The path exists, but not with this HTTP method. Both operations are `POST` requests.
x-enumDescriptions.tool_rate_limited: 429. The API key has read about 250 dashboards in this workspace in the last 24 hours.
x-enumDescriptions.tool_unavailable: 503. The dashboard can't be read now.

message.description: What went wrong, in English, for a person to read. Don't check it in code, because it can change.
message.example: The tool call cannot be run as it is.

details.description: More about the error. On `invalid_tool_call`, each wrong field and what it must be. On `token_incomplete`, the missing or invalid token claim, in `claim`. Absent on the other codes.
